# DB cutoff tradeoff — universe size vs benchmark accuracy per source

## Figure legend — Supplementary Figure 1

> **Supplementary Figure 1.** Re-deriving each source database’s surface-inclusion rule against SurfaceBench changes which proteins two of the five sources admit, while the other three are left unchanged. Each panel shows one source database; points are alternative inclusion rules of increasing permissiveness, plotted by the number of proteins each would admit (horizontal axis, log scale; further left is stricter) against accuracy on SurfaceBench (vertical axis). Points are annotated with sensitivity and specificity. The original rule and the rule adopted after the benchmark audit are marked. UniProt was loosened by additionally accepting transmembrane- and signal-peptide-annotated entries, recovering GPI-anchored and single-pass receptors it had been missing with little loss of specificity. CSPA was tightened by restricting it to high-confidence detections only, improving specificity at comparable recall. Human Protein Atlas and SURFY were already at their optimum and left unchanged; GO was left unchanged because its accuracy gain did not justify the extra proteins admitted.
<!-- END manuscript-legend -->

For each of the five source databases in the candidate-universe vote
(UniProt, GO CC, HPA, SURFY, CSPA), a small panel plotting how the
choice of surface-inclusion cutoff trades universe size (proteins the
rule admits, log-scale x) against accuracy on the 147-protein
benchmark (y, %). Further left = stricter. HPA abstains on benchmark
proteins it has no data for, so its panel is scored on the 98
benchmark proteins HPA covers; the other four panels use all 147.

Markers:
* Diamond ("Original rule") — the database's pre-audit inclusion rule.
* Star ("Adopted after benchmark audit") — the rule adopted after the audit, shown only where it
  differs from the original (UniProt "TM+signal" and CSPA "HC-only").
  The candidate-universe vote now uses these two rules.
* Circle — other cutoffs that were evaluated and not adopted.

The table under each panel lists, for every cutoff: its short label,
universe size (`n=`), and `+X/-Y`, where X is the % of benchmark
surface proteins it recovers and Y is the % of benchmark non-surface
proteins it correctly excludes (specificity, not recall).

Run:

```
uv run make_db_cutoff_tradeoff.py
```

Data (bundled in this gist):

- Precomputed trade-off points (small TSV):
  [`data/processed/triage_bench/db_cutoff_tradeoff_points.tsv`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/data/processed/triage_bench/db_cutoff_tradeoff_points.tsv).
  The script reads the copy that sits next to it in the gist and
  falls back to the in-repo copy only when that bundled file is
  missing. The TSV is a committed artifact: the figure scripts only
  read it. It is regenerated deliberately by running
  `DUMP_CUTOFF_POINTS=1 uv run python scripts/figures/triage_bench_db_barplot.py`
  ([`scripts/figures/triage_bench_db_barplot.py`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/scripts/figures/triage_bench_db_barplot.py)).

Canonical in-repo generator:
[`scripts/figures/db_cutoff_tradeoff.py`](https://github.com/Deliverome-Project/accessible-surfaceome/blob/main/scripts/figures/db_cutoff_tradeoff.py).
The accuracy math ran once over the raw database source dumps to
build the points table; both this gist script and the canonical
generator plot from that table.
